SYM and Alt shortcuts that open apps and commands
Hold SYM or Alt and press a letter to open what is assigned to it. Both use the same assignment list.
Smart toggle: Alt off after an opening
With Alt locked, typing an opening quote or bracket with Alt (\" ( [ {) switches Alt off, so the words inside come out as letters
Smart toggle: Ctrl off after a shortcut
A tapped Ctrl switches off after one shortcut such as copy, paste or undo; cursor and selection moves keep it on
Show dev-build updates, calibration, debugging and preview tools. On in dev builds
Trackpad debug and the release notes preview
Dev-build updates and tools for calibrating, debugging and previewing the keyboard. Most people never need them.
Termux and other terminals: Alt and SYM type symbols, Ctrl stays Ctrl

A terminal tells keyboards it has no text field, so Alt and SYM would go to the terminal and Flux Keyboard\'s symbols wouldn\'t work. In terminal mode Flux Keyboard types into it like a text field without suggestions, corrections or automatic capitals: Alt and SYM type Flux Keyboard\'s symbols, and Ctrl, held, tapped or latched, reaches the terminal as a real Ctrl (Ctrl+C, Ctrl+D…). Enter, Backspace, Tab, Esc and the arrows go to the terminal as they are.
In the apps below: Alt and SYM type Flux Keyboard\'s symbols, Ctrl stays Ctrl
Learn nothing from anything you type: no new words, predictions, emails or numbers, and no recent emoji, symbols or GIFs
Learn nothing in fields that ask keyboards not to, such as private browser tabs
For a minute after you copy text, a new text field offers it as a suggestion; typing dismisses it. Text marked sensitive (a password manager\'s) is only offered in password fields
A password field offers what you just copied, including from a password manager, as ⎘ •••••••• (never the text itself). It\'s kept in memory only, never in the clipboard history
An emoji for the word you\'re typing, e.g. 🍕 for pizza. Picking it adds the emoji after the word.
Underline misspelt words in every app using Flux Keyboard\'s dictionaries, including words you added. Tap to choose Flux Keyboard in Android\'s spell checker settings.

Make your own Device SYM layer: what each key types with SYM, and with Alt when Alt uses the Device SYM layer. A profile can replace a keyboard\'s own layer automatically, and Flux Titan Hub\'s backup includes it.
Tap a key to set what it types. Leave it empty to type nothing.
That file isn\'t a Device SYM profile.
Save this profile as a JSON file you can import on another phone.
Send this profile as text to another app.
Keyboards it replaced go back to their curated profile.
Use instead of the curated profile on:
Only where you choose it (Alt layer)
Make your own Device SYM layer, blank or from a curated profile.
Your own Alt and SYM characters for every key, in a custom Device SYM profile. Ctrl shortcuts are under Key shortcuts.
No profiles yet. Start one above.
Arrow keys, selection and more from the letter keys, with Ctrl
Your password manager\'s saved logins, one-time codes and addresses appear as chips in the suggestion bar; tap one to fill the field.
One colour for all LEDs from the theme, or a colour for each
Off: all LEDs use the theme\'s LED colours.
Each LED has its own colour: dim when off, the colour when active, brighter and more saturated when locked.
Tap an LED to change its colour
Active: held, or the emoji layer · Locked: tapped for one symbol, or the symbols
Active: held · Locked: tapped for one symbol, or the symbols
Active: held · Locked: tapped for one emoji, or the emoji layer or picker
Back to the suggested blue, orange, green and purple.
Emoji for chatting, work, social media, food, travel and more; or your own
A profile puts 26 emoji on the emoji layer, one per letter key, for a situation. Apply one to make it your emoji layer; edit single keys in Customize SYM layers.

The emoji layer follows the app you\'re in: Chatting in messengers, Social media in social apps, Work in work apps, Food and drink in food apps, Travel in maps and travel apps. Other apps keep your own layer.
Save the emoji layer as a profile
Keep the emoji layer as it is now, to switch back to later.
From a profile shared from Flux Titan Hub.
That file isn\'t an emoji layer profile.
No keyboard bar in any app. The keys work as usual (Alt layer, SYM, Ctrl shortcuts, corrections), and the emoji and symbols pages still open on their keys.
The status LEDs still show where they usually are, drawn over the app, so you can see Shift, Alt, Ctrl and SYM.

Swipe across the keys to move the terminal\'s cursor a character at a time; swipe up or down for the commands before and after (the arrow keys). Nav Mode (double-tap Ctrl) works in terminals too: its keys move the cursor there.
With the keyboard hidden, its status LEDs still show where they usually are, so you can see Shift, Alt, Ctrl and SYM.
Like the Linux desktop: Flux Keyboard stays out of sight in terminals. Alt still types your Alt layer and SYM its symbols, unseen; Ctrl stays Ctrl. The clipboard and emoji picker show while open.
A locked modifier\'s LED sweeps a gradient between its colour and a more intense version, so a lock is hard to miss.
What your emoji key does in terminals
Extra keys: Esc, Tab, Ctrl, Alt and arrows in the bar\'s place
Show or hide the extra keys row

Esc, Tab, Ctrl, Alt and arrows in the bar\'s place, from the menu, a shortcut or the emoji key in terminals. While the row is open, Q to P press its keys, left to right. Terminals and other apps each have their own set.
Pick up to %1$d keys, in the order you want them. The letter beside each is the key that presses it.
The terminal\'s Alt (hold with another key)
Use this profile for the Device SYM layer on every keyboard.
This is your Device SYM layer now.
Edit this symbol layer. Hold to edit variations.
Apps where what you type stays as typed: SSH, code, AI agents

In these apps nothing rewrites what you type: no auto-correct, text replacements, auto-capitals, double-space full stop or automatic spaces. Suggestions still show, and only change a word when you pick one.
Also where apps ask for no suggestions
Fields that tell keyboards not to suggest (code editors, terminals, some search boxes) get exact typing too
Choose an app where every character should stay as typed
The row that opens with ☰. Switch buttons on or off; the higher a button is in this list, the further left it sits. The close button always comes first.
Move up (further left in the bar)
Move down (further right in the bar)
Suggestion bar words in bold, easier to spot at a glance
Links you copy lose their tracking (utm_, fbclid, YouTube\'s si…) right on the clipboard, so they\'re clean wherever you paste them, and open the full site rather than the mobile one
Ctrl+Shift+Q, W or E: the left, middle or right suggestion
Ctrl+1, 2 or 3: the left, middle or right suggestion (number row)
Recent emoji first on the layer
The emoji you used last take the layer\'s first keys, and its own emoji move along. Emoji you type from the layer count too.
A pick you undo straight away makes swipes need a little more; a swipe that falls short before a pick makes them need a little less.
Suggestion swipes back to your setting
After %1$d s without typing, a swipe scrolls instead of picking
Turn Scroll assistant on: the phone only passes keyboard swipes to Flux Keyboard while it\'s on. Leave Swipe mode on scrolling: custom swipe actions take the swipes for themselves.
The phone\'s spell checker in suggestions
When Android\'s spell checker is another app\'s (Gboard\'s, say), its corrections for a misspelt word join the suggestion bar.
The built-in shell, root or Shizuku, for gaming mode, streaming and the shell extras
These run as the ADB shell, through the built-in shell or Shizuku. Flux Titan Hub only runs the commands each option needs.

Lets Shizuku turn on wireless debugging and start itself after a restart, without root: Flux Titan Hub grants it the permission it needs (write secure settings), then opens Shizuku so you can turn on Start on boot in its settings.
Shizuku can start itself at boot: turn on Start on boot in Shizuku\'s settings if it isn\'t already. Tap to open Shizuku.
Done: in Shizuku, turn on Start on boot (wireless debugging)
Shizuku couldn\'t be given the permission. Is Shizuku running?
The shell didn\'t answer the check. Make sure the built-in shell (or Shizuku) is running, then look again.
The phone has no keyboard light service (agui_functional_service).
Checks for the keyboard light again, and starts following the screen if it\'s found.
This phone\'s keyboard light can\'t be reached through the shell (the Titan 2\'s can).
Stays lit after a key press
On and off with the screen
The keys light up when the screen turns on and go dark when it turns off.
A brighter screen makes brighter keys, and they dim and fade with it.
The keyboard flashes three times for a new notification (needs notification access).
Force-stop the app in front, Battery Saver on or off, and the app in front off the network (Android 14 and later): assign them to keys in Key shortcuts, or find them in the quick launcher.
Assign the shell shortcuts to keys.
Or put them on keys pressed on the home screen.
Or on Ctrl keys in Nav Mode.
On a rooted phone: shell commands run through su instead of the built-in shell or Shizuku, ready at boot without pairing or Wi-Fi.
Root wasn\'t granted: the built-in shell or Shizuku is used instead.
Through root, the keyboard\'s LEDs are set in their own steps, much finer than the light\'s usual levels, so following the screen\'s brightness has no visible steps.
This game has its own trackpad, screen and stick settings.
Uses %1$s\'s settings. Turn this on if this game needs different ones.
Set to shell access, the trackpad\'s swipes are read straight from the keyboard.
Shell access lets codes be read from notifications Android hides from apps (Android 15 and later).
Shizuku isn\'t running yet. Start it in Shizuku (Start via Wireless debugging), then come back and try again.
Shizuku remembers Flux Titan Hub being refused, so it won\'t ask again. In Shizuku, open Authorized applications and switch on Flux Titan Hub.
This Shizuku is too old to ask. Update it from Shizuku\'s GitHub page, then try again.
Shizuku didn\'t show its question. In Shizuku, open Authorized applications and switch on Flux Titan Hub.
The built-in shell isn\'t running, and neither is Shizuku. Set up the built-in shell above, or start Shizuku, then come back.
In games with a profile, your keys play as a controller or tap the game\'s on-screen buttons.

The keyboard isn\'t a controller: it has no real sticks, and its keys and the volume keys do all the work, so gaming mode suits games that play on buttons. Your mileage may vary. For the best experience, use a controller over Bluetooth or USB, ideally one made for a phone held upright or one with a phone clip.
See and change which keys are which buttons
Each key shows the button it is, alone or with the modifier chosen here held. Tap a key to change it.

Changed keys are outlined. For games played only by touch, keys can also be placed on the game\'s screen: Place keys on screen, in gaming mode\'s notification while the game is open. A placed key taps there instead.
Nothing (goes to the game as it is)
Every key back to the layout\'s button
Press the key on the keyboard (with a modifier held if you like), or tap it below.
Dolphin reads the keys from its own settings: changes here are written there the next time a Dolphin game starts from Games or Gaming settings opens.
Each button shows the keys that press it. Tap a button to pick its key, alone or with a modifier: the keys that pressed it before then press nothing.

Left stick: W A Z D (S clicks it)
D-pad: right Shift + W A Z D
Right stick: left Shift + I J M L, or SYM + W A Z D (K clicks it, SYM + S too)
Face buttons: I (Y), J (X), M (A), L (B)
Bumpers: Q and E
Triggers: Volume Down (left) and Volume Up (right) (Alt + Volume: pressed all the way without the click, for a GameCube controller)
Start: Space
Select: Shift + Space
Xbox / Home: Alt + Space
Volume: SYM + Volume Up or Down

Keys placed on a game's screen tap there instead.
Creates Download/Flux Keyboard/Games with a folder for each launcher and emulator. ES-DE\'s ROMs folder is read too.

Created in Download/Flux Keyboard/Games. For GameNative, go to Settings > Interface > Frontend Sync and choose the GameNative folder. For the official GameHub, set its Export for frontend to the GameHub folder.
A folder you already use in a launcher or emulator.
None of the launchers or emulators Flux Titan Hub can start games in is installed (GameNative, GameHub, GameHub Lite, Dolphin, PPSSPP, Azahar, Eden).
The game rotates the screen as it likes. In GameNative, turn on Portrait mode in the game\'s settings (General) to play upright.
The game gets a landscape screen while you hold the phone upright, and the screen doesn\'t turn. Best for most games. It\'s slightly shorter, to stay clear of the camera.
The game gets the whole upright screen, whatever it asks for. For DS and 3DS emulators (their two screens one above the other), phone games made for portrait, and vertical arcade games.
Nintendo\'s layout: M presses B, L presses A, I presses X and J presses Y, so each key presses the button in its place. On by default for Nintendo emulators.
The last app a game ran in (%1$s) has no profile. Some launchers run games in a separate app: add it to the launcher\'s profile so gaming mode stays on during play.
From GameNative, GameHub or your game folders, each with a home screen shortcut, or a game you added to a launcher or emulator yourself.
No games found. Add a game to the home screen from its launcher, or add the launcher itself.
How far the pointer moves when you slide your finger. It moves on from where it is, not to where you touch.
GameNative\'s games only take sticks from a real controller or its on-screen controller, so your keys move the on-screen sticks (kept invisible).

In GameNative, once per game:
1. Start the game and open its menu (Back).
2. Turn on the On-screen Controller, with its default layout.
3. Set Control Opacity to 0.

Your keys then move its sticks (W A Z D, and Alt with I J M L). To press its buttons, place keys on them from the gaming mode notification.

To play with the phone upright, turn on Portrait Mode in the game's settings, General.
Your home screen doesn\'t accept shortcuts.
Drag each key onto the game\'s button, and each circle onto its stick. Add a key, then press it or pick it.
Allow Flux Titan Hub to display over other apps, then try again.
Ticked, a layer opens on your recents. Unticked, it opens on its default page (Developer\'s pick until you change it with the pencil in its bottom-left corner), with your recents one page back on Q.
Running. Shizuku and Termux aren\'t needed. After a restart it starts by itself once Wi-Fi connects. USB debugging stays on: Android stops the shell when debugging is fully off.
Paired, not running yet. It starts by itself once Wi-Fi connects. Tap to start it now.

Set it up once with wireless debugging, and Flux Titan Hub needs neither Shizuku nor Termux. Tap, then in Wireless debugging tap Pair device with pairing code, and type the code into Flux Titan Hub\'s notification. Android 11 and later.
It didn\'t start. Connect to Wi-Fi, or turn on Wireless debugging, and try again.
Allow Flux Titan Hub\'s notifications first: the pairing code is typed into one.
The built-in shell stops starting by itself. It keeps running until the next restart.
In Wireless debugging, tap Pair device with pairing code.
Pairing timed out. Try again from Flux Titan Hub\'s settings.
Type the six-digit code Wireless debugging shows.
That code didn\'t work. Check it and try again.
Done. The built-in shell is running, and starts by itself after each restart once Wi-Fi connects.
Paired, but the shell didn\'t start. Make sure Wireless debugging is on, then tap Built-in shell in Flux Titan Hub\'s settings.
Shizuku is running but hasn\'t allowed Flux Titan Hub yet.
Allow Flux Titan Hub in Shizuku
Shizuku asks once; these options show after you allow it.
The app in front off the network, or back on
Nav Mode on, and every move extends the selection
Incognito typing and Offline mode together
Private mode on: nothing is learned or remembered, and nothing goes online
Private mode off: typing and Offline mode are back as they were
Pauses don\'t end dictation: it carries on sentence by sentence until you tap the mic or stay silent
A few settings that suit nearly everyone: modifiers, suggestions, LEDs and, on the Titan 2 Elite, its trackpad and compact bar. Matters of taste stay yours.
Your settings already match the recommended ones.
Recommended settings applied. Go through your choices (auto-correct, GIFs, colours), the extras that need a permission, and making it yours? It takes a minute, and you can skip it.

plurals.name: recommended_settings_differ
plurals.item: %d of your settings differs from the recommended ones. Applying replaces it, along with the recommended mappings and variations. Back up first if you might want yours back.
%d of your settings differ from the recommended ones. Applying replaces them, along with the recommended mappings and variations. Back up first if you might want yours back.

resources.string: Your keys play as a controller (see Keyboard controls). For touch-only games, place keys on its buttons from the gaming mode notification.
Your keys play as a controller in %1$s (see Keyboard controls). Keys you place on screen tap there instead.
Press Back again to leave the game
Pick a key below, or press it.
Recording… move two fingers on the trackpad
If both sticks won\'t move at once: tap, then move a finger on each half of the trackpad for %1$d seconds. Saved to Download/Flux Keyboard/trackpad-test.txt so you can share it.
Most fingers seen at once: %1$d (%2$s).\n\nSaved to Download/Flux Keyboard/trackpad-test.txt.
Shows your games in the quick launcher, opening them the same way as their home screen shortcuts.

%1$s\'s controls now follow Flux Titan Hub\'s keyboard controls (see Keyboard controls).\n\nDolphin: GameCube controller 1 (L and R on the volume keys, Z on E) and Wii Remote 1 with Nunchuk are set, the pointer following the trackpad\'s right half. PPSSPP: its controls are set for every game.
Couldn\'t find %1$s\'s settings. Open it once, then try again.

%1$s can\'t load controls from a file. In its Settings, under Input (Controls), bind each button by pressing its key when asked:
%2$s
Give the %1$s\'s buttons and movements keys of this game\'s own, such as a wheelie button. Kept as a Dolphin profile for this game.
Tap a button to give it a key, alone or with a modifier. Buttons with this game\'s own key are outlined, and a key given here presses only that button.
Saved. Dolphin uses it from the next time this game starts from Games.

Applied each time this game starts from Games: its controller, keys and on-screen controls go into Dolphin then, with nothing to set in Dolphin. Opened from Dolphin itself, a game plays with the controls of the last game started from Games. Invisible on-screen controls are needed for sticks and keys placed on the screen.
This game plays with the controls set here, even if a profile was chosen for it in Dolphin. Off: a profile chosen in Dolphin is kept.
Invisible (for sticks and keys placed on them)
Change which key is which button here alone, on top of Keyboard controls. Works in any emulator or launcher gaming mode sends buttons to.
Keys changed here apply only while this plays, on top of Keyboard controls. Each key shows its button, alone or with the modifier chosen here held. Tap a key to change it.
No games yet. Add one with Add a game, or create the game folders in Gaming settings.
Adds a Games app to your app list (Niagara too) with all your games. Long-press it to jump to a game.
Add every game to the home screen
A home screen shortcut with its art for each game with a profile. The home screen asks for each one.
Found among your games. Set up its controller, screen and sticks now, or play it with %1$s\'s settings.
Controller keys in the Games app

Move through the Games app with the same keys as in games: W A Z D to move, M to open, J for a game\'s settings, L to go back, Q or E to switch between games and launchers, Space for gaming settings. A controller works too.
Set up gaming mode for it: controller, screen and sticks.
Plays in Flux Titan Hub\'s own player. Sign in once, then your keys work as a controller in every game.
Play Xbox Cloud Gaming in Flux Titan Hub\'s own player (the Xbox apps don\'t stream on phones). Pick a game from the catalogue: it gets its own settings and opens straight into the game.
Couldn\'t load the catalogue. Check the phone is online and offline mode is off.
Sign in to Xbox in Flux Titan Hub\'s player. Once signed in, every cloud game plays.
Adds it to the Games app and Moonlight\'s list without playing it. Games you play are added by themselves.
In your games: in the Games app and Moonlight.
The XCloud catalogue lists only the cloud games your plan includes, from Microsoft\'s own Game Pass lists.

Lists the phone in Moonlight on any device on the same network. Pair with the PIN Moonlight shows: the phone\'s screen, Android\'s desktop and your games appear there, XCloud games included. Moonlight\'s Wake starts streaming on the phone if it\'s off.

Keeps the phone listed in Moonlight while streaming is off, so you don\'t need Wake (some Moonlight apps, like the one for LG webOS, send their Wake where the phone can\'t hear it). Picking a game turns streaming on. Pair once with streaming on first.
%1$d paired. Each will need the PIN again.
%1$s is visible in Moonlight on this network.
Android\'s record of Flux Titan Hub\'s last crashes, saved to Download/Flux Keyboard/crash-log.txt to share.
Empties the phone\'s logs and Flux Titan Hub\'s own record, so the next crash log holds only what happens from now and saves quickly.
Unihertz\'s Game Mode can take over as the home screen alongside gaming mode. Turn it off here.
Covers show in the Games app and Moonlight; square artwork on shortcuts and in settings.
Use a picture from the phone
Graphics: %1$s, native resolution, shaders built in the background (things may appear a moment late instead of stuttering), dual core on, VSync off. Raise the resolution in Dolphin for lighter games.
Graphics: %1$s, 2× resolution, shaders built in the background, dual core on, VSync off.
Graphics: %1$s, 2× PSP resolution, no frame skipping, hardware transform and skinning on.
Graphics: %1$s, 3× PSP resolution, no frame skipping, hardware transform and skinning on.
What to change in its own settings for smooth play
In Azahar\'s Settings, Graphics: Graphics API %1$s, Internal resolution 1×, Disk shader cache on, Asynchronous shader compilation on. Lighter games can take 2×.
In Eden\'s Settings, Graphics: Resolution 0.75× (1× for lighter games), Accuracy Normal, Asynchronous shaders on, Disk shader cache on.

In Eden\'s Settings, Graphics: Resolution 0.5×, Accuracy Normal, Asynchronous shaders on, Disk shader cache on. This phone\'s Mali GPU runs fewer Switch games than Adreno phones do: check reports for a game first.

In %1$s, the game\'s (or its container\'s) settings: Graphics driver %2$s, DXVK for DirectX 9 to 11 games (WineD3D if one won\'t start), VKD3D for DirectX 12, Screen size 1280×720, Box64 preset Performance.
In the game\'s own settings: graphics quality Medium or Low, a 60 fps limit only if it stays steady (else 30), and render scale or resolution below 100% if it offers one.
Automatic streams at the resolution set in Moonlight on the client, 4K included. Choosing a size runs what\'s streamed at that size and lets the client scale it up, which is easier on the phone.
It wants to stream from this phone.
It wants to play %1$s from this phone.
Don\'t ask again for this device

Mirror shows the phone\'s screen on the Moonlight client. Separate screen runs the app or game on its own screen for the client and leaves the phone free; the Games app shows it on the phone and sends your keys, touches and placed keys to it. Android desktop does the same with Android 16\'s desktop, switching desktop windowing on for you (a restart may be needed the first time). You can switch between them from the streaming notification.
Desktop windowing is now on. If the desktop doesn\'t show, restart the phone once.
Send keyboards, mice and controllers to the stream
Keyboards, mice and controllers connected by USB or Bluetooth control what\'s streamed instead of the phone. They go back to the phone when the stream ends.
Show the phone\'s screen in Moonlight
Adds the phone\'s screen to Moonlight\'s list, to show whatever is on it.
Signed in to Xbox in Flux Titan Hub\'s player.
Cloud games won\'t play until you sign in again.
Puts everything Flux Titan Hub changed in %1$s (controls, graphics, per-game controllers) back how it was. Changes made by older versions of Flux Titan Hub can\'t be undone.
%1$s\'s settings are back to how they were before Flux Titan Hub changed them.
When kept upright, the game renders at this height and is scaled up to fill the screen. Lower runs smoother.
No artwork found online. Try searching for its title above.
The official GameHub can only be opened, not told which game to start. Install GameHub Lite alongside it: the games the official GameHub exports then start straight away in GameHub Lite.

GameHub Lite has no Export for frontend. Install the official GameHub alongside it and set its Export for frontend to the GameHub folder in Download/Flux Keyboard/Games: its games are then listed here and start in GameHub Lite.

Written into %1$s\'s settings as a game starts from Games (an app\'s also now, for games started in %1$s itself). Screen is set to suit it: Portrait for one above the other, Landscape for the rest. The trackpad\'s bottom-screen area follows it. Catch: if you\'ve used Swap Screens in %1$s, the screens come out the other way round, so swap them back there.
Written into NooDS\'s settings now. NooDS reads them when it opens, for every game: it has no settings per game. Screen is set to suit it.
%1$s keeps its screen layout in its own private settings, which Flux Titan Hub can\'t reach: set it in %1$s\'s settings or in-game menu.
Cemu shows the Wii U GamePad\'s screen from its in-game menu (Show pad), placed where its settings say (General). It keeps both in its private settings, so Flux Titan Hub can\'t set them per game.
Keys on it now (tap one to take it off):

The Moonlight client gets the stream\'s sound whatever this is set to. Media sound off turns the phone\'s media volume to nothing while a stream plays; All sounds off also silences notifications, the ringer and the phone\'s own sounds (calls and messages vibrate). Alarms still sound. Everything goes back as it was when the stream ends.
Find a Moonlight client on the Wi-Fi (LG webOS for now). Flux Titan Hub can then turn it on and open Moonlight straight into a game you pick on the phone.
%1$s: picking a game while streaming can stream it there. Tap to find it again or forget it.
Looking for Moonlight clients on the Wi-Fi…
No Moonlight client found. It needs to be on and on the same Wi-Fi (LG webOS for now).
%1$s is set up. Pair Moonlight on it with this phone once, if you haven\'t.
Couldn\'t set up %1$s. Check it\'s on, then try again.
Flux Titan Hub turns this Moonlight client on and opens Moonlight on it into the game you pick. For turning it on, it needs Turn on via Wi-Fi (or Mobile TV On) in its settings.

Ask each time: opening a game while streaming asks whether to stream it to the Moonlight client (turned on, Moonlight opened straight into the game) or play it on the phone. With streaming off, games play on the phone.
Streaming is on. Streamed: %1$s is turned on and Moonlight opens there, straight into the game.
%1$s didn\'t answer. Turn it on, or turn on Turn on via Wi-Fi (Mobile TV On) in its settings.
%1$s didn\'t allow Flux Titan Hub. Accept it there when asked.
Moonlight couldn\'t be opened on %1$s. Is Moonlight installed there?
This game isn\'t on the phone any more

Your keys as a controller, and the Games app

Stream the phone\'s screen, Android\'s desktop (a second screen for any app) or your games to a Moonlight client. Off, the phone no longer answers Moonlight; pairings are kept.
Keyboard light and shortcuts, through Shell access
What every module shares. A module\'s own settings are on its page: tap its tile on the home screen.
Gaming mode sends keys and touches to games through it.
Streaming shares the screen and passes on Moonlight\'s controls through it.
The extras below run through it.
Paired, not running yet: tap to start it.
Not set up yet: tap to set it up once, no root needed.
Screen sizes are set through it.
Default, Tablet or Desktop for the whole phone, and a size per app
Tap an app to open it on the TV while you stream. Long-press one to list it in Moonlight too.
Adds a Streaming app to your app list (Niagara too) to open any app on the TV while you stream.
Adds a Keyboard app to your app list (Niagara too) that opens this page.
